title: Question 2
stem:
An ideal gas initially has pressure 1.0 × 10^{5} Pa, volume 4.0 × 10^{-4} m^{3} and temperature 300 K, as
illustrated in Fig. 2.1.
A change in energy of the gas of 240 J results in an increase of pressure to a final value of
5.0 × 10^{5} Pa at constant volume.
The thermodynamic temperature becomes T.

parts.label: (a)(i)

markscheme_points.text: p ∝ T or pV / T = constant or pV = nRT

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in ideal gas laws and thermodynamics that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: p ∝ T or pV / T = constant or pV = nRT; T (= 5 × 300 =) 1500 K
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Ideal gas laws and thermodynamics. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
p ∝ T or pV / T = constant or pV = nRT; T (= 5 × 300 =) 1500 K
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
